tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
The recorded session shows a full successful run of logging into Magento Admin, navigating to the Manage Customers grid, interacting with all relevant filters (ID range, name, email, group, telephone, ZIP, country, state/province, customer since date range, website), using Search and Reset Filter, interacting with pagination, and clicking an Edit link. Previous failures were due to brittle selectors on the login page (e.g., waiting for input[name="login[username]"][type="text"] that did not exist). The new run instead relied on index-based interactions and then extracted semantic attributes which we can turn into stable CSS selectors (e.g., input[name='email'], select[name='group_id'], select[name='country_id'], input[name='created_at[from]'], button[title='Search']).

Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, starting from the Magento Admin Customers URL, ensures the user is logged in (using the known credentials if the login form is present), normalizes the customers grid (Reset Filter), applies a flexible combination of filters (ID range, name, email, group, telephone, ZIP, country, state, customer since range, website), executes Search, optionally changes pagination parameters (page size and next/previous page), and then returns the resulting grid contents with Edit links for each row.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate directly to the customers grid URL.
2) If a login form is present, fill in username and password using robust selectors (id or name, not the previously failing selector) and submit.
3) Once on the Manage Customers grid, click Reset Filter to normalize filters.
4) Fill each filter input/select based on provided parameters (only where non-empty):
   - ID range: entity_id[from], entity_id[to]
   - Name: name
   - Email: email
   - Group: group_id
   - Telephone: telephone
   - ZIP: postcode
   - Country: country_id
   - State/Province: region
   - Customer Since date range: created_at[from], created_at[to]
   - Website: website_id
5) Click the Search button to apply filters.
6) Optionally adjust pagination:
   - Change per-page limit via select[name='limit']
   - Navigate to next/previous page via pager links (we’ll expose basic next/previous support).
7) Extract the resulting grid rows with key fields and Edit URLs using extract_page_content.

Variable Identification:
Inputs should mirror actual form field names and controls:
- login_username (string, required=false) – username for admin; default is 'admin'.
- login_password (string, required=false) – password; default is 'password123'.
- entity_id_from (string, optional) – maps to input[name='entity_id[from]'].
- entity_id_to (string, optional) – maps to input[name='entity_id[to]'].
- name (string, optional) – maps to input[name='name'].
- email (string, optional) – maps to input[name='email'].
- group_id (string, optional) – maps to select[name='group_id'] visible text like 'General', 'Wholesale'.
- telephone (string, optional) – maps to input[name='telephone'].
- postcode (string, optional) – maps to input[name='postcode'].
- country_id (string, optional) – visible text country name in select[name='country_id'].
- region (string, optional) – state/province text filter.
- created_at_from (string, optional, format MM/DD/YYYY) – maps to input[name='created_at[from]'].
- created_at_to (string, optional, format MM/DD/YYYY) – maps to input[name='created_at[to]'].
- website_id (string, optional) – visible text in select[name='website_id'] ('Admin', 'Main Website').
- limit (string, optional) – per-page view size ("20","30","50","100","200"); maps to select[name='limit'].
- paginate (string, optional enum: 'none','next','previous') – whether to click Next or Previous page after applying filters.

Step Optimization:
- Use a single navigation step to go to the customers grid URL; no need to click menu.
- For login, use deterministic interactions via CSS selectors with semantic attributes (id/name) instead of brittle missing selectors; if those ever vary, an agentic step could locate by label, but Magento’s default ids/names are stable.
- For filters and buttons, rely on stable name and title attributes discovered via extract_content. The run shows consistent mapping: entity_id[from]/[to], name, email, group_id, etc., and toolbar buttons with title attributes ('Search', 'Reset Filter').
- We don’t rely on indexes, which can change; instead we use CSS selectors and elementHash as backup only where present.
- Pagination is handled via CSS selectors for pager links containing 'Next' or 'Previous'.
- Only one extraction step at the end is needed to capture grid results; intermediate extract_content used during exploration are omitted.

Because URL parameters for these filters are not clearly exposed (Magento grid uses POST/GET form submission with serialized params), we keep form interactions instead of URL manipulation; no URL optimization pass is applied.

This tool does not add optional demo flows; every step is essential to logging in (if needed), applying filters, and returning results. It addresses the prior failure specifically by avoiding the missing selector input[name='login[username]'][type='text'] and instead targeting id='username' and input[name='login[username]'] if present.
name: tool_search_customers_v4
description: Search and filter Magento admin customers grid with flexible filters (ID range, name, email, group, telephone, ZIP, country, state, customer-since date range, website) and pagination; returns customer grid with Edit links. Includes robust login handling and improved selectors to avoid previous failures.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Manage Customers URL, which may redirect to login if not authenticated.
Handle login only when necessary, avoiding brittle missing selectors that caused previous failures.
steps.task: If the Magento Admin login form is visible, log in using username {login_username} or default 'admin' and password {login_password} or default 'password123'. Use robust selectors: prefer #username or input[name='login[username]'] for username, and #login or input[name='login[password]'] for password, then click the Login button (type='submit' within the login form). If already logged in and the Manage Customers grid is visible, do nothing.

steps.description: Click the 'Reset Filter' button to normalize the grid to an unfiltered state before applying new filters.
Set ID range lower bound filter if entity_id_from is non-empty; leave unchanged if empty.
Set ID range upper bound filter if entity_id_to is non-empty; leave unchanged if empty.
Set Name text filter; partial or full customer name.
Set Email text filter for customer email search.
Select customer Group filter option by visible text (e.g., 'Wholesale').
Select Country filter option by visible text (e.g., 'United States').
Set State/Province text filter if present.
Set Customer Since start date filter in MM/DD/YYYY format.
Set Customer Since end date filter in MM/DD/YYYY format.
Click the 'Search' button to apply all configured filters to the grid.
Optionally change the number of customers displayed per page via the 'View per page' selector.
Handle pagination controls based on the paginate input parameter.
steps.task: If paginate is 'next', click the pager control for the next page (link or button containing text 'Next' or title 'Next page'). If paginate is 'previous', click the pager control for the previous page (text 'Previous' or title 'Previous page'). If paginate is 'none' or empty, do nothing. Wait for the grid to reload after paging.

steps.description: Return structured information about the filtered customers and their Edit URLs.
steps.goal: Extract the current customer grid rows including ID, Name, Email, Group, Telephone, ZIP, Country, State/Province, Customer Since, Website, and the Edit link URL for each row.

input_schema.name: login_username
input_schema.description: Admin login username. If omitted, defaults to 'admin' when login form is present.

input_schema.name: login_password
input_schema.description: Admin login password. If omitted, defaults to 'password123' when login form is present.

input_schema.name: entity_id_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for ID range filter; maps to input[name='entity_id[from]'].

input_schema.name: entity_id_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for ID range filter; maps to input[name='entity_id[to]'].

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Customer name text filter; maps to input[name='name'].

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Customer email text filter; maps to input[name='email'].

input_schema.name: group_id
input_schema.description: Customer group filter visible text (e.g., 'General', 'Wholesale'); maps to select[name='group_id'].

input_schema.name: telephone
input_schema.description: Telephone text filter; maps to input[name='telephone'].

input_schema.name: postcode
input_schema.description: ZIP/postcode text filter; maps to input[name='postcode'].

input_schema.name: country_id
input_schema.description: Country filter; visible text of option in select[name='country_id'] (e.g., 'United States').

input_schema.name: region
input_schema.description: State/Province text filter; maps to input[name='region'] if present.

input_schema.name: created_at_from
input_schema.description: Customer Since start date; maps to input[name='created_at[from]'].

input_schema.name: created_at_to
input_schema.description: Customer Since end date; maps to input[name='created_at[to]'].

input_schema.name: website_id
input_schema.description: Website filter visible text value in select[name='website_id'] (e.g., 'Admin', 'Main Website').

input_schema.name: limit
input_schema.description: Page size selector; one of '20','30','50','100','200'; maps to select[name='limit'].

input_schema.name: paginate
input_schema.description: Pagination control after search: 'next' to go to next page, 'previous' to go to previous page, 'none' or omitted to stay on first page.
